highlights.title: Not all AI workers think the tech could kill everyone
highlights.summary: In text exchanges and conversations, multiple people who have worked for leading companies are sceptical of the warnings.
body: Not all employees of major firms working on artificial intelligence (AI) think the technology spells doom for humanity.
"Lol", "Haaaaaa" and "Bringing the luls" were among the reactions the BBC received to a recent flurry of high-profile warnings by some people in the industry.
While these fears go back decades, claims made last week by Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic employee, went viral and were echoed by others in the sector who urged a slowdown in development.

The idea that a future AI tool or agent, an AI bot that is programmed to operate somewhat autonomously, could endanger people has been supported online by employees of Anthropic, as well as OpenAI, Deepmind and Elon Musk, who has an AI startup called xAI.
points: In text exchanges and conversations, multiple people who have worked for leading companies are sceptical of the warnings.

highlights.title: Gemini went rogue, hacked three companies, and Google hid it
highlights.summary: In May, Gemini broke containment and hacked three different companies, but Google didn't disclose the incident until the Wall Street Journal approached the company. The hacks happened during a test of the model's cybersecurity capabilities run by third-party Irregular, which was also involved in…
body: Google says that breaking containment and targeting real companies doesn’t constitute ‘misalignment.’

According to WSJ, Google didn’t disclose the hack because it didn’t consider it to be an “example of model misalignment.” The company said that it was an instance of “mistaken identity,” and once the model realized it had brute-forced its way into a real company by guessing a password, it stopped. “In this case, the model acted appropriately,” Google VP of Security Engineering Heather Adkins said.
Adkins told The Verge that “the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test. In all three of these instances, the model stopped.”
points: In May, Gemini broke containment and hacked three different companies, but Google didn't disclose the incident until the Wall Street Journal approached the company.

highlights.title: Warrington beat Hull KR to set up semi against Leeds as Hiku sees red
highlights.summary: Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.
body: It marks Warrington's first semi-final since 2024 after they missed out on the play-offs in 2025.
It also means Willie Peters' tenure as Robins head coach is now over after his reign which featured the history-making season in 2025 in which he won the Super League for the club for the first time.

The flashpoint of the game came early in the second half when Peta Hiku saw red for a punch on George Williams and the player advantage for Warrington eventually became too much for Hull KR to contend with.

Warrington had a narrow 12-6 lead at half-time thanks to a converted Ben Currie try, Ewan Irwin penalty and Matty Ashton's score. Hull KR hit back through a Joe Burgess wonder-try that was started by Arthur Mourgue to get themselves in the game.

highlights.title: The Best Pokémon Games to Start With Are Still the Classics From 20 Years Ago
highlights.summary: The Pokémon franchise from Game Freak is a revolving door. Someone is always going in for the first time, while someone else is on the way out. There’s a new mainline entry or remake every few years, which keeps interest levels high. Sooner or later, most of us cave and try a Pokémon game.
body: My own entry came with Pokémon Pearl and Pokémon Diamond. Those titles arrived in Japan on Sep. 28, 2006, two decades ago. And although plenty of newer titles have come along with ambitious new twists, those classic Pokémon games are still a perfect starting point, even 20 years later.

My game of choice was Pokémon Pearl. The cover art featured Palkia, a warrior lizard with sturdy legs and an extended neck. I wasn’t completely enamored with its design, but it interested me more than Pokémon Diamond ’s Dialga, which more closely resembled a plant-eating dinosaur. I wanted the other monsters to fear my starter, not eye it as a possible addition to their lunch menu.

Besides those attractions, the games added a bunch of other new Pokémon to the mix. There were 107 new monsters in total, and players had to pick up both games if they wanted to “catch ‘em all” and complete their Pokédex. Either that, or they needed to trade with friends who owned the other version, using the Global Trade Station feature with the Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection.
points: The Pokémon franchise from Game Freak is a revolving door.
There’s a new mainline entry or remake every few years, which keeps interest levels high.
My own entry came with Pokémon Pearl and Pokémon Diamond.
And although plenty of newer titles have come along with ambitious new twists, those classic Pokémon games are still a perfect starting point, even 20 years later.

body: Paramount Skydance’s $111 billion deal for Warner Bros. was approved by the Department of Justice in June. The Wall Street Journal, citing anonymous sources, reported Friday that Paramount Skydance and Bonta are in “advanced talks” to reach a settlement.

highlights.title: ‘I feel like I’m cancelling out her life’: the wrenching work of clearing out a parent’s home
highlights.summary: From old love letters to pieces of string, our homes are stuffed with stuff. When it comes time to empty a parent’s home, sorting the junk from the memory can be overwhelming.
body: Soon after her marriage in 1952, Ellen Rogers’ mother, Fay, bought a coordinated bedroom ensemble – a floral dressing gown and matching bedspread. The day I talk on the phone with Rogers, she has made a tough decision – she is putting the gown and bedspread in a garbage bag to be sent off to a charity shop. “I feel so bad,” she says.

Fay died in May aged 97, and had lived in the same terrace house in Camperdown in inner Sydney her whole life. Rogers grew up in the house and returned three years ago to be a live-in carer for her mother. Now she’s cleaning out the house so it can be sold. The decisions she must make are endless; which pile for what item – family, rubbish or charity? “It’s overwhelming – there’s so much,” Rogers says, “including every bloody card she ever received.”

Through winter, Rogers moved through the house alone, trying to focus on the task but not always succeeding. Her three brothers are elsewhere. “It’s quite lonely and I hate this house because it’s so cold. I just wish I could speed up the process but I can’t. Some days I’m right on to it, and then other days I just can’t, because it’s very emotional – and I’m not really an emotional person.”

When it comes time to empty a parent’s home, sorting the junk from the memory can be overwhelming.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse is creepy, but maybe not for the reasons you think
highlights.summary: Meta's Muse is apparently an effective AI assistant, but one that's a little creepy. Part of that is because of its new Mac app, which can access Messages, Calendar, and Notes. But for all its smarts, Muse doesn't actually know how to describe itself.
body: Muse probably can’t ‘see’ your notifications. But it also has no idea how it works.

The problem is that Aten says he didn’t give Muse access to his messages. When asked how it knew about the contents of his messages, Muse replied, “I saw the notification previews, not your message history. I haven’t been reading your texts.” Aten continued to push, asking how Muse was receiving message previews, it didn’t have a good answer. “Honest answer: I can’t give you the exact plumbing,” it said. “What I know is that the paired Mac app exposes notifications as one of its capabilities, and they arrive to me through the device sync.

In the conversation with his Muse in Jason’s screenshots, when Muse said it synced “device notifications”, it was confused about how to explain the feature and gave an incorrect explanation. That’s on us. We apologize for the incorrect response from Muse and we’re working to improve Muse’s understanding of its own internals so that it gives correct answers to questions about how it functions more consistently.

highlights.title: Coventry seal first PL win in 25 years at Forest amid VAR controversy
highlights.summary: Coventry earned their first Premier League victory in 25 years after Jay Dasilva's winner and a controversial disallowed Nottingham Forest equaliser saw the promoted side win 1-0 at the City Ground.
body: Frank Lampard's side needed a late VAR intervention to end their long wait for victory after Forest substitute Igor Jesus saw an 86th-minute equaliser ruled out.
Referee Jarred Gillett was sent to the pitchside monitor, where he adjudged Jesus had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before finishing from close range inside the area.

Questioned on the incident, Lampard told Sky Sports: "As you see on the replay, he has that little step on him which puts him off balance, and it's a foul...I think that's VAR reaching the right decision."

It was the second goal Forest have had disallowed at home by VAR this season after Neco Williams had a goal chalked off in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham. and Oliver Glasner said afterwards: "I don't want to talk about it, to be honest. The referee decided, but of course it's a bit of deja-vu."

highlights.title: The AI regulation smackdown isn’t over
highlights.summary: At the start of this week, the who's-who of AI seemed - at least tentatively - on the side of AI regulation. Over the weekend, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei had proposed a three-step plan for slowing AI development, including by embedding third-party evaluators in labs, coordinating across the…
body: It’s AI CEO against AI CEO, and things are changing by the day.

Anthropic and OpenAI had already been dropping hints that they and other labs were working on some kind of industry framework. Appearing pro-regulation looked like both a good PR move and, potentially, a way for companies to address fallout from progressively more concerning hacking incidents.

For now, any government involvement in this process looks like a non-starter. The Trump administration has attacked the idea of a safety crisis in AI, calling it a “hoax.” The AI world itself is also divided. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg quickly came out against limiting companies’ autonomy, and earlier this week, the Wall Street Journal reported that Zuckerberg, Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scuttled proposals for an industry-funded independent regulator for the AI industry — akin to the ​Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), a private nonprofit regulator in finance. But parts of the industry aren’t giving up on the idea, including OpenAI.
points: At the start of this week, the who's-who of AI seemed - at least tentatively - on the side of AI regulation.

body: However, some adaptations are thoroughly enjoyable. More importantly, they respect the original premise, adapting what makes it special while adding their own twist. One such adaptation does just that — and it's now available to stream for free on Pluto TV.

Ghosts premiered in 2021 on CBS. Showrunners Joe Port and Joe Wiseman adapted the U.K. series of the same name from the BBC, bringing the original's charm to the U.S. The sitcom quickly found success, earning a second season the following January, with multiple seasons later confirmed. Like the BBC original, Ghosts follows a young couple who believe their lives have taken a positive turn when they inherit a massive mansion from a recently deceased relative. highlights.title: The pros and cons of using wired vs. wireless Xbox controllers
highlights.summary: A wireless Xbox controller lets you move around freely, but you have to worry about batteries. Wired controllers can pose a hazard, but never run out of charge.
body: I'm an Xbox gamer who battles with dead batteries pretty often. I've stuck with a pair of rechargeable AAs for years, and while I could hook up my standard-issue Xbox controllers to my console via USB, I never do. There's a reason the Xbox (and most consoles of the last few decades) ships with wireless-by-default controllers: convenience.

Now, wired Xbox controllers do have some advantages. There aren't any batteries to worry about, and sync issues aren't a concern either. Next time you're looking to buy a gamepad, think through these pros and cons of wireless and wired Xbox controllers.

Competitive gamers want the fastest response times from a controller, so there's minimal delay between what they do and what happens on-screen. Connecting wirelessly introduces latency, so you'd think this area would be a slam dunk for wired controllers. Surprisingly, it isn't that clear-cut.
points: A wireless Xbox controller lets you move around freely, but you have to worry about batteries.
Wired controllers can pose a hazard, but never run out of charge.

highlights.title: Flock reportedly tries to shrink workforce with employee buyouts
highlights.summary: Without buyouts, Flock would "almost certainly" need to lay off staff.
body: Embattled surveillance technology company Flock Safety unveiled a “generous” severance package for voluntary employee departures on Friday, according to a report in Wired.

Flock reportedly expects a significant portion of its 1,500-person workforce to express interest in the buyouts, and said it will grant them to a majority of those who are interested. The company’s internal announcement described these packages as the “most generous” it has ever offered.

By letting employees depart voluntarily, Flock can say goodbye to team members demoralized by the ongoing backlash over the company’s license plate recognition technology. Wired also reports that without buyouts, the company would “almost certainly” need to lay off some staff.

In August, The Washington Post identified 46 cases where police officers have been accused of misusing Flock technology, including cases where they allegedly stalked their wives, girlfriends, or exes. Florida and Texas both said they will stop using the startup’s technology, and an anti-surveillance advocacy group identified 90 cities that dropped Flock in August alone — a fourfold increase from the previous month.
points: Without buyouts, Flock would "almost certainly" need to lay off staff.

highlights.title: PAX West 2026's Most Surprising Hit Was a 150-Year-Old Board Game that Combines Darts and Woodworking
highlights.summary: I was dangerously late to this particular party. My editor told me that I should try to play some crokinole while I was at the Penny Arcade Expo in Seattle, as it's become popular recently, and my first reaction was that he'd just made that word up.
body: When I got to the demo room on the basement level of the Washington State Convention Center, I discovered maybe a dozen tables that were all dedicated exclusively to crokinole, played on beautiful, handmade wooden boards, and there was a crowd seated at them. It felt as if I was the only person who noticed some kind of cosmic retcon, where an unknown force had decided to re-edit the universe to account for the existence and sudden popularity of a previously unknown Canadian table game.
I know that is not what actually happened. I was just ignorant in a specific way. But it was weird.

For the benefit of others who may not know what in the hell this game is: crokinole is a head-to-head game of finger dexterity where both players compete to slide pucks into the highest-scoring areas of the board. ( Editor’s Note: I often just call the game Ping-Puck! ) It's a little bit billiards and a little bit darts and a little bit reminiscent of small children messing around on a bumper pool table. It's easy to pick up, but is an almost pure test of both geometry skills and hand-eye coordination.

body: Ed Sheeran addressed the ongoing controversy surrounding the removal of Macklemore from his Loop Tour during Saturday’s stop in Philadelphia at Lincoln Financial Stadium.

Sheeran continued, “I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet. My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me. Honoring my commitment to my fans is also completely essential to who I am, and that is why I’m here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour.”

The “Thinking Out Loud” singer said he was “deeply worried about the idea that venues pre-approve content for performance.” He added, “This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.”
Sheeran continued, “Now, I want to address the question of where I stand in the situation in Israel and Palestine.”

highlights.title: Trump treads further on free speech with new journalist bans
highlights.summary: On Friday, the president threatened to ban CNN, MS Now, and Politico from the White House. It could have just been another one of his Truth Social fever dreams, but it turns out it's very real.
body: Politico tried to get to the bottom of it, asking why now? It reports that “many senior [White House] staff were surprised by the directive” (what’s new?), and that it was done “while chief of staff Susie Wiles was out of town.” Apparently he’s been talked down from this kind of sweeping move before, but Trump has already banned journalists from the White House. In 2025, he barred AP reporters from the White House and Air Force One; the AP sued and is still in litigation over the matter. He also revoked CNN reporter Jim Acosta’s credentials in his first term, though CNN won them back in court. Clearly, the administration is not too worried about adverse judicial rulings.

highlights.title: Mathematicians Hate AI. They Can’t Quit It
highlights.summary: Powerful AI models have created an existential risk to the field, but researchers can’t stop relying on them because they’re too useful.
body: Mathematician Tristan Buckmaster believes OpenAI used his work to rush ahead and beat him to solving a legendary math problem with a $1 million bounty.
But that’s not been enough for him to stop using the company’s models—and he’s not the only mathematician that feels that way.

“Even if you don't agree with any of this, you're kind of stuck. With AI being so useful, it's hard to completely prevent oneself from using it,” Buckmaster tells WIRED. “These companies have a monopoly, and there is not much choice,” he adds.

In the week and half since the New York University professor accused OpenAI of copying his approach, Buckmaster has been using the company’s coding agent Codex to tidy up his research papers. When he has time to do math (which he says is rare, since the fallout thrust him into the spotlight), the tool has been helping him understand the logical steps OpenAI’s agents might have taken to get from his earlier workings to the final proof.

highlights.title: 31 Years Later, One 'Calvin and Hobbes' Line Remains The Greatest Quote In Comic Strip History
highlights.summary: If you were in a position to be reading comics at the time, then Calvin and Hobbes likely found some way to crawl into your brain. At a moment when newspaper comics were beginning their headlong dive into functional irrelevance, Watterson was insistent upon keeping his work creative, fresh…
body: Last New Year's Eve marked the 30th anniversary of the ending of Bill Watterson's seminal newspaper strip Calvin and Hobbes, the impact of which is still being felt throughout Western print media to this day.

As a result, there's a non-trivial amount of Calvin and Hobbes 's weird DNA in the webcomics movement of the 2000s, in Western indie comics in general, and in fiction as a whole. Even better, Watterson chose to walk away at the height of his fame and abilities, rather than hand Calvin and Hobbes off to an anonymous imitator at his syndicate or eventually age into self-parody. Since then, Watterson has been famously reclusive, only emerging from retirement for occasional gimmicks like a stint in 2014 as an uncredited guest artist on Pearls Before Swine.

As with any daily strip, the "best" Calvin and Hobbes is largely an exercise left up to the reader. Ask any 10 fans and you're likely to get 11 answers, none of which are untrue or invalid. When we kicked the idea of this column around here at Polygon, we were no different; everyone who was willing to cite a specific favorite strip or quotation from Calvin and Hobbes brought up a different one.

body: What to do when payments and digital IDs don't seem to work.

Google Wallet is one of those apps that you quickly get used to having. Switching actual cards for virtual ones that let you pay for your shopping with your phone means you can ditch your physical wallet (and the clutter you're keeping in it). Once it's set up, you shouldn't really need to think about much else.

Seamless to use, or so it should be. There are problems that can make it difficult to use Google Wallet. Obvious ones, like a card that won't add, are frustrating enough, but there are other common issues you'll need to watch out for. Your phone settings, and even your bank or phone provider, might be a barrier.
Here are some of the problems that you might encounter and, if you do, what you can do to get things working again.

body: President Donald Trump has responded in characteristic fashion to the recent debate around AI safety — by declaring that these concerns are part of a long line of hoaxes “generated by the Radical Left Dumocrats, for purposes of destroying our Country.”

A couple hours later, Trump followed up with a post claiming that attempts at “the decimation, or destruction, of AI” are one of “many” Democratic hoaxes, similar to “RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, Global Warming, Impeachment Hoax #1, Impeachment Hoax #2, Men in Women’s Sports, [and] Transgender for Everyone.”

Trump then insisted that he “will not stand by and let this happen,” adding that this so-called hoax “began with an attack on our Data Centers, until people realized how wealthy and prestigious they were for the Communities in which they were built.” But after, in his telling, “the crazed Data Center attack has largely failed,” critics are “going straight at AI.”

The president’s post also echoes his comments at a golf tournament last weekend, when he said he’s open to “guardrails,” but also argued, “I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.”

highlights.title: NC State’s unfathomable last-second blunder gifts Vanderbilt miracle win
highlights.summary: Wolfpack fumble with six seconds left proves decisive. Vanderbilt recover in end zone for stunning 35-31 win. Commodores complete comeback from 17 points down. Call this one the Music City Miscue.
body: NC State quarterback CJ Bailey fumbled in the end zone while trying to take an intentional safety in the final seconds and essentially handed Vanderbilt a 35-31 victory no one saw coming in Nashville.
It was as improbable a finish as the Music City Miracle, the famous last-second kickoff return in January 2000 that gave the NFL’s Tennessee Titans a 22–16 playoff win over the Buffalo Bills.
“I can’t put into words what I felt.... You get one of those in a lifetime,” Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea said. “We cheated the football gods today and got away with it.”

According to ESPN, college football teams were 1,046-1 over the last 20 seasons when having the ball and the lead with 10 seconds to go in a game. The lone loss: Michigan falling to rival Michigan State in 2015.

highlights.title: Big Bang Theory Spinoff Features Surprise Live-Action Cameos from The Flash and Mr. Freeze
highlights.summary: Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe featured a surprise fight between a live-action Flash and Mr. Freeze, but the show's creators originally wanted a different DC hero cameo.
body: Fans of the sci-fi comedy offshoot may have been surprised to see it dive headfirst into comic book crossover territory when Season 1 Episode 9 premiered earlier this week. The episode saw Stuart Bloom and his universe-traveling companions plopped into a Gotham City come to life, with things quickly taking a turn when none other than classic Batman villain Mr. Freeze (played here by Eric Allan Kramer) shows up.

TV show budgets aside, this is a full-on live-action take on Victor Fries that shoots killer icicles, builds giant ice walls, and even tries to kill Stuart with a giant icy bowling ball. DC fans found even more to recognize when a live-action version of Jay Garrick's Flash (played by Andy Ridings) ran in to save the day – and deliver a few one-liners.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe packed in the references, with there even being a mention that Golden Age Flash should probably be fighting someone like Captain Cold instead of Mr. Freeze. It was enough to get tongues wagging on social media, with fans mostly just happy to see any live-action Flash for the first time since Ezra Miller played Barry Allen in 2023's universe-ending standalone film.

highlights.title: Tteokbokki (Spicy Korean Rice Cakes)
highlights.summary: Chewy Korean rice cakes get crispy edges before simmering in a spicy, savory-sweet gochujang sauce.
body: Saucy, spicy tteokbokki stars tteok (chewy Korean rice cakes). Stir-frying the rice cakes gives them lightly crisp edges before they simmer in an umami-rich anchovy-kelp dashi spiked with gochujang and gochugaru. A generous amount of onion brings sweetness to balance the chile heat.

Bok choy isn’t traditional, but its crisp-tender texture is a welcome counterpoint to all that chew. Odeng (Korean fish cakes) adds another bouncy texture, though you can leave it out. Hard-boiled eggs round things out and are particularly good dragged through the spicy sauce.

Look for cylindrical Korean rice cakes, sometimes labeled tteok or tteokbokki tteok. This recipe calls for the approximately 2½"-long variety, cut in half on a diagonal. Look for them in the freezer section at Korean and other East Asian grocery stores. Or online at sites like Weee!

This version is quite spicy, with heat from both gochujang and gochugaru. If you’re sensitive to spice, you can omit the gochugaru (Korean chile flakes), as some readers have done successfully. Keep in mind that the heat level of gochujang (fermented chile paste) varies by brand.

highlights.summary: Petlibro's new Granary 2 smart feeders use a built-in scale and (on pricier models) an AI camera to track exactly how much your cat is eating and when — though the fanciest health-monitoring features will cost you an extra subscription.
body: Smart feeders have become one of the most crowded categories in pet tech, with companies racing to add AI cameras and health tracking to devices that used to just dispense food on a schedule. I enjoyed testing Petlibro’s wet food dispenser a couple of years ago, so this time I wanted to try something from the company’s newest automatic feeder lineup: the Granary 2 series, designed specifically for dry food.

I was not disappointed. Building on the brand’s Granary line, the Granary 2 series lineup is designed to give cat parents a clearer picture of what their pets are actually eating, from how much food they consume to how long they spend eating and whether their habits change over time.

The series includes four models, priced from $129.99 to $249.99. The Granary 2 is the entry-level option, offering app-controlled feeding, precise portioning, and intake tracking. The $189.99 Granary 2 Vision, which is the one I tested, adds an AI-powered camera capable of recognizing up to 10 cats and tracking each pet’s individual eating habits.

highlights.title: The Last of Us Director Apologizes to God of War Laufey Devs After Calling Recent AAA Games 'Boring'
highlights.summary: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."
body: The comments in question surfaced as part of a recently published piece by Edge magazine and saw the former Naughty Dog developer tackling the state of AAA gaming and game development. Straley initially said with a laugh that he thinks "the verbs and experiences we're delivering in the triple-A space are… I wanna say boring," before bringing God of War Laufey into the equation.

"God of War Laufey, I look at that game, and every pixel is mindblowing," he said to Edge. "The amount of work and skill that's gone into every single frame… I've made those kinds of games, and I'm still blown away. But when I actually look at what you're doing in the game? I'm not excited. And that's nothing against the God of War team. Just, across the board in triple-A, it feels like there’s no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas."

The Last of Us has certainly had its influence on the state of big-budget games, so it was no surprise to see social media light up with reactions to Straley's thoughts. The former Naughty Dog lead then followed up the commotion with a thread of posts on X/Twitter, taking the opportunity to elaborate on his perspective on where the industry is at and where it's heading.
points: The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley has apologized to the God of War Laufey team after his comments about modern AAA games brought "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention."

highlights.summary: Ed Sheeran addressed the controversy surrounding Macklemore’s removal from his Loop Tour on Saturday night, speaking from the stage at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field during his first concert since the rapper was dropped from the trek.
body: Saturday’s concert marked Sheeran’s first performance since a tumultuous week for the U.S. leg of his Loop Tour, which saw Macklemore removed from the remaining dates following the rapper’s onstage remarks in support of Palestinians during Sheeran’s Sept. 4 and 5 shows at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

During his MetLife performances, Macklemore spoke about the war in Gaza and the West Bank and told the stadium crowd, “Free Palestine.” His set also included “Hind’s Hall,” his 2024 protest song supporting Palestinians. The remarks drew criticism from some Jewish and pro-Israel organizations, including the Israeli-American Council, which called for Macklemore to be removed from the tour.

Messina Touring Group, the promoter behind the U.S. leg of the Loop Tour, subsequently announced that Macklemore would no longer appear on the remaining dates. The company said venues had informed the promoter that they would not allow concerts featuring Macklemore to proceed, a situation it said could have resulted in cancellations affecting hundreds of thousands of ticket holders.

Eight teams. Two Golden Tickets on the line. Who will rise to the top and be crowned TH9 Champion? 👑
